messages:
Dinesh: quick sync — we need a short dashboard to track KV/prefix cache behavior + token-level latency breakdown per route. hitting a regression on 2.4.1 kernel selector and I want visibility before rollback
Alice: +1. what's the minimum set of panels you want?
Dinesh: per-route KV hit rate, eviction rate, memory footprint, reuse_by_route (how many requests reuse cached prefixes), and token latency breakdown into: kernel_time, batching_wait, kv_lookup, decode. also a heatmap for longest tail tokens.
Ben: can we derive reuse_by_route from existing labels? we have route, model, kernel_version on the kv metrics. reuse_by_route would be: count(kv_reused{route=~".*"}) / count(requests{route=~".*"})
Carla: agreed. I'll add a small PromQL panel. Draft queries:
```
# hit rate by route
sum(kv_hits_total) by (route) / (sum(kv_hits_total) by (route) + sum(kv_misses_total) by (route))
# evictions per minute
rate(kv_evictions_total[5m]) by (route)
# mem bytes by route
sum(kv_mem_bytes) by (route)
# reuse ratio
sum(kv_reused_total) by (route) / sum(requests_total) by (route)
```
Carla: we should tag those with model and kernel_version for rollout correlation.
Dinesh: +1 tag kernel_version. critical for triage. also add a panel that shows kernel_selector decisions over time (which kernel chosen for seq length buckets).
Eva: I can emit kernel_selector_decision{kernel="...",seq_bucket="0-128"} from runtime agent. will add to the agent next deploy.
Ben: for token latency breakdown we already instrument per-token spans in profiler. Prometheus export names? we have token_span_seconds_bucket, but need to break by span_kind (kernel, batch_wait, kv_lookup, decode).
Dinesh: exact names we want in dashboard: token_latency_kernel_p50/95/999, token_latency_batchwait_p50/95/999, token_latency_kv_p50/95/999. we can compute with histogram_quantile on the token_span histogram filtered by span_kind.
Carla: sample query for p95 kernel time: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_span_seconds_bucket{span_kind="kernel"}[5m])) by (le, route, kernel_version))`
Alice: can we also show end-to-end per-token latency broken down so SREs can see if kernel or batching is the culprit when latency spikes?
Dinesh: yes — two stacked bars: kernel vs batch_wait vs kv vs decode (p95). Also a line for total p95.
Infra-bot: deploy queued: runtime-agent v3.7.4 -> canary (infra). ETA 10m
Eva: pushed metric change to agent branch, tests pass. will cut canary in 15.
Ben: small gotcha: when we started using the new kernel_selector heuristic last week, kv_lookup time increased for small-batch fast-path because we changed cache key format. that might explain the regression.
Dinesh: can you surface that in debug logs or metric? maybe a metric kv_key_format_version so we can correlate.
Ben: added kv_key_format_version gauge on the canary host. good call.
Carla: dashboard panels list I'm going to create:
- KPI row: global kv_hit_rate, global_eviction_rate, kv_mem_bytes
- Per-route table: hit_rate, evictions/min, mem_bytes, reuse_ratio, recent_eviction_examples (link to logs)
- Token latency breakdown (p50/p95/p999) stacked by span_kind per route
- Kernel selector timeline: kernel chosen by seq_bucket and model
- Regression alert: if route_hit_rate drops >8% or p95 token latency increases >30% over baseline (30m window) -> pager
Alice: for baselines, use 14-day rolling median. prefer alert to reference baseline label to avoid noisy false positives.
Dinesh: also add annotation when we roll kernel_selector commits — commit hash should be in trace so dashboard can link to commit.
Eva: agent will emit runtime_build_hash and kernel_selector_commit label.
Carla: I'll create a Grafana dashboard and add to dashboards repo under runtime/kv-prefix. naming: runtime_kv_prefix_v2.
Dinesh: thanks. one more ask: add reuse_by_route heatmap over last 24h with columns = hour, rows = route, value = reuse_ratio. helps spot routes that never reuse cache.
Ben: ack. will wire reuse_ratio into the aggregations.
Alice: want a quick runbook blurb for SREs: if p95 spikes -> check kernel_selector timeline, reuse ratio, eviction spikes, and kernel_version. If eviction spike + low mem -> memory pressure on node.
Dinesh: perfect. Carla, can you have a first-pass dashboard + runbook stub by EOD?
Carla: yes. will open PR with dashboard json + runbook.
Dinesh: thanks everyone, will monitor canary and watch the new panels. :eyes:
Infra-bot: canary deployment started: runtime-agent v3.7.4 on canary pool.
Eva: canary metrics already showing kv_key_format_version=2 on two hosts.
Ben: initial profiler stats from canary: kernel p95 unchanged, batch_wait p95 down 12%, kv_lookup p95 up 22% on small-routes. shipping queries now to dashboard to validate.
Dinesh: if kv_lookup regression confirms, we'll rollback the key-format change and instead opt for a mapping layer. but let the dashboard surface it first.
Alice: thanks, keeping an eye. :thumbsup:
